mainEntity.name: What is the best clipboard manager for Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose Maccy for a free, open-source, focused clipboard history. Choose Paste for organized history synced across Mac, iPhone, and iPad. Choose Raycast if you already use its launcher. Choose Gojo when clipboard history belongs beside files, windows, media, and other notch controls.

mainEntity.name: Is Maccy or Paste better for privacy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maccy says clipboard data is stored on your computer and that it is open source. Paste says history stays on your devices and in private iCloud, not on Paste servers, and supports exclusions for sensitive apps. The right choice depends on whether local-only storage or cross-device sync matters more.

mainEntity.name: Does Gojo keep clipboard history locally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gojo keeps clipboard history local to the Mac and skips content marked private by supported password managers. Gojo's public product materials do not document cross-device clipboard sync or a permanent retention period.

blocks.text: What a clipboard manager needs to answer

content.s: Clipboard history is a record of things you copied. That can include a harmless URL, but it can also include a password, recovery code, customer message, or private file. Compare where history is stored, how long it stays, which apps can be excluded, and whether your workflow needs text only or images and files too. A bigger history is not automatically safer.

blocks.text: 1. Gojo for clipboard history inside a broader Mac workflow

content.s: Gojo keeps recent copied text available in a searchable clipboard history inside the notch workspace. It skips content marked private by supported password managers. The useful distinction is placement: you can recover a copied line while the same surface also handles window controls, file staging, media, dictation, and display comfort. Gojo is not the right pick if you need a documented cross-device archive or a deep clipboard-only tool.

items: Gojo is a native macOS 14+ utility.
Clipboard history is local to the Mac.
Gojo's public materials do not document a fixed retention limit, image OCR, file previews, or iPhone and iPad sync.

blocks.text: 2. Maccy for a small, focused history

content.s: Maccy does one job: keeping copy history at hand. Its official site says it is lightweight, keyboard-first, stored on your computer, and open source under the MIT license. That narrow scope is its appeal. You do not buy a larger workspace to get a clipboard. You give up Gojo's surrounding notch tools and any cross-device sync that Maccy does not publicly document.

blocks.text: 3. Paste for an organized history across Apple devices

content.s: Paste is the clearest choice when the same snippets need to follow you from Mac to iPhone and iPad. Its official site documents searchable history, pinboards, and private iCloud storage rather than Paste-hosted storage. That convenience brings a different privacy boundary than a local-only manager. If your work policy does not allow clipboard sync, choose a local option instead.

Raycast bundles clipboard history with app launching, commands, snippets, extensions, and window management. Its clipboard documentation lists text, images, colors, and links, plus local encryption and default exclusion of password-manager content. The free plan lists three months of history. Longer retention and unlimited history belong to Pro. Choose Raycast when the launcher is already your main entry point, not because every clipboard job needs a command palette.

items.q: What is the best clipboard manager for Mac?

a.s: Maccy is the best focused free option. Paste is strongest for Apple-device sync. Raycast suits launcher users. Gojo fits people who want clipboard history as one part of a broader MacBook notch workspace.

items.q: Is Maccy or Paste better for privacy?

a.s: Maccy says clipboard data stays on your computer and its source is open under MIT. Paste says history stays on your devices and in private iCloud, not on Paste servers, and supports app exclusions. Local-only and private-cloud sync are different choices, so use the one your workflow allows.

items.q: Does Gojo support clipboard images and files?

a.s: Gojo's public product materials document searchable recent copied text and local history. Image handling, file previews, OCR, and a cross-device clipboard are not publicly documented. Choose Raycast or Paste if those documented content types are central to your workflow.

items.q: Can I use Gojo and Maccy together?

a.s: Yes, but decide which app should own clipboard history so you do not create duplicate capture streams. Maccy can handle dedicated keyboard-first recall while Gojo handles other notch controls.
